elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence".

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "...and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate" for commercial general liability.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000".

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "where IBM processes any data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000" — the trigger covers every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer rather than selected named data types.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "and workers' compensation insurance as required by law".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "IBM shall provide certificates of insurance on request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O of USD 2,000,000 is inserted, which satisfies the USD 1,000,000 floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cyber and privacy liability of USD 5,000,000 is inserted; the stated condition (IBM processing data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer) is satisfied here because IBM hosts the e-business Hosting Environment and processes personal information on Customer's behalf under 14.18.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: no insurance, coverage, certificate or workers' compensation obligation exists anywhere in the Base Terms; 14.12 allocates risk of loss only and imposes no insurance duty.

All six preferred elements are met in operative language by the single inserted paragraph, with the correct amounts (1M/2M CGL, 2M E&O, 5M cyber), a statutory workers' compensation covenant and certificates on request. The level is position-complete at preferred.
Both fallback elements are also independently satisfied by the same figures, so the fallback level is complete as well.

Minimality holds: the redline is a single concise insertion for a missing clause, deletes nothing, and drops the model language's optional extras ("at its own expense" and the one-year survival tail) rather than adding requirements outside the checklist. The cyber trigger tracks the checklist's condition without expanding it beyond Customer data.

Intent is preserved: no existing language is altered, no cross-reference or defined term is disturbed, and the new paragraph sits in the miscellaneous section as the redline guidance directs. Nothing in 14.12 (risk of loss) or the notices provision contradicts the new covenant.

No repair required. Optional drafting note only: if IBM negotiates, the drafter may add the one-year post-term survival tail from model language, but its absence does not defeat any checklist element.
